# FD1797_02 - Floppy disk formatter/controller, single and double density, true data bus, side select output (FD1797-02)

Package DIP-40 · family MOS LSI · catalogue file [catalog/chips/FD1797_02.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/FD1797_02.json)

## Functions

| Output pin | What it does |
|---|---|
| 7-14 | Data access lines: three-state buffers, drivers when CS and RE are low, receivers when CS and WE are low. A1 A0 with RE: 00 status, 01 track, 10 sector, 11 data register; with WE: 00 command, 01 track, 10 sector, 11 data register. |
| 38,39 | DRQ: set when a byte is assembled into the data register (read) or the data register has moved to the shift register (write); cleared when the computer reads or loads the data register; also status bit 1. INTRQ: set at the end of every command and by a met Force Interrupt condition; cleared by reading status or writing a new command. |
| 15-18,25,28-31,33 | Disk interface outputs: STEP/DIRC for head positioning at the rate in r1 r0, HLD head load, TG43, WG and WD for writing with EARLY/LATE precompensation, SSO side select, VFOE for the external data separator. Their sequence is given by the command flow charts on pages 9-16. |

## Stored state

Changes on: CLK; register writes (WE) and reads (RE); disk inputs

- Command summary (bits 7..0): Type I Restore 0000hVr1r0, Seek 0001hVr1r0, Step 001uhVr1r0, Step In 010uhVr1r0, Step Out 011uhVr1r0; Type II Read Sector 100mF2EF10 (F1 = S side select, F2 = b sector length flag on 1795/7), Write Sector 101mF2EF1a0; Type III Read Address 11000E00, Read Track 11100E00, Write Track 11110E00; Type IV Force Interrupt 1101 I3 I2 I1 I0.
- Type I flags: h = 1 load head at beginning; V = 1 verify on destination track; r1 r0 stepping rate; u = 1 update track register.
- Stepping rates r1 r0 = 00/01/10/11: 3/6/10/15 ms at CLK 2 MHz, 6/12/20/30 ms at 1 MHz (TEST = 1); with TEST = 0: 184/190/198/208 us at 2 MHz, 368/380/396/416 us at 1 MHz.
- Verify: after a 15 ms settling time (30 ms at 1 MHz, none with TEST = 0) HLT is sampled; the first ID field track number is compared with TR; match with valid CRC ends without error; no match sets Seek Error (status 4); CRC error sets status 3 and the next ID is read; no valid ID within the stated revolutions ends with Seek Error.
- Restore: if TR00 is low, TR = 0 and interrupt; else steps out until TR00 goes low, then TR = 0; after 255 steps without TR00 it ends with Seek Error. Restore is also executed when MR goes from low to high.
- Seek: TR holds the current track, DR the desired track; steps until TR = DR.
- Type II/III flags: m = 1 multiple records; a0 = 1 write deleted data mark F8, 0 data mark FB; E = 1 15 ms delay before HLT is sampled; S (1795/7) sets SSO; b (1795/7) sector length table: b = 0 gives 256/512/1024/128 bytes for length field 00/01/10/11, b = 1 gives 128/256/512/1024.
- Read/Write Sector: READY must be high; finds the ID with matching track, sector, side and CRC within 5 index pulses or sets Record Not Found; the data address mark must come within 30 bytes (FM) or 43 bytes (MFM) of the last ID CRC byte; a byte not taken in time sets Lost Data; Write Sector writes zeros (6 FM, 12 MFM), the data mark, the data, 2 CRC bytes and one byte of ones, then WG off; m = 1 increments SR and continues until SR exceeds the sectors on the track or a Force Interrupt.
- Read Address: reads the next ID field (track, side, sector, length, CRC1, CRC2) through DR with a DRQ per byte; the track address is written into SR.
- Read Track: from the leading edge of an index pulse to the next, every byte to DR with a DRQ, gaps included, no CRC check, byte sync on each address mark.
- Write Track (formatting): DRQ at once; writing starts at the next index pulse and ends at the following one; DR bytes F5-FE are written as address marks with missing clocks, F7 writes two CRC bytes (control byte table page 14).
- Force Interrupt: I0 not-ready-to-ready, I1 ready-to-not-ready, I2 every index pulse, I3 immediate interrupt; all zero terminates the command without an interrupt. It is the only command that clears the immediate interrupt on a later command load or status read.
- Status after Type I: S7 not ready (inverted READY ORed with MR), S6 write protect, S5 head loaded (HLD AND HLT), S4 seek error, S3 CRC error, S2 track 0 (inverted TR00), S1 index (inverted IP), S0 busy.
- Status after Type II/III: S7 not ready, S6 write protect (writes), S5 record type on read (1 deleted data mark) or write fault on write, S4 record not found, S3 CRC error, S2 lost data, S1 data request (copy of DRQ), S0 busy.
- HLD: set at the start of a Type I command with h = 1 or near the end with V = 1, and on any Type II or III command; it stays active until a Type I command with h = 0 and V = 0, or after 15 index pulses while idle.

| outputLowMaxCurrentMa | 1.6 |
| outputHighMaxCurrentMa | -0.1 |
| inputSchmitt | no |
| notes | DC characteristics (page 18), TA 0..70 C, VDD +12 V +-0.6 V, VCC +5 V +-0.25 V: VIH 2.6 V min, VIL 0.8 V max, VOH 2.8 V min at -100 uA, VOL 0.45 V max at 1.6 mA; input leakage 10 uA, output leakage 10 uA; power 0.5 W max. VDD 10 mA nominal, VCC 35 mA nominal. Absolute maximum VDD and any input -0.3..15 V. DRQ and INTRQ are open drain and need 10K pull-ups. |

## Not known

- The data sheet is a preliminary specification with tentative parameters (page 24).
- Output high current: only VOH 2.8 V at -100 uA is given, used as outputHighMaxCurrentMa; no separate drive rating.
- Whether STEP, DIRC and the other disk outputs are push-pull is not stated; stored as totem-pole because only DRQ and INTRQ are called open drain.
- The number of revolutions allowed for a Type I verify: the text on page 9 says four revolutions, page 6 says 5 revolutions; both are in the source.
- Register contents after power-on other than those loaded by MR (command 03, sector 01) are not stated.

## Notes

Card 3207 part FD1797. The family sheet covers 1791-1797; 1797 = double density, true data bus, write precompensation, side select output (family table page 1). Only 1797 facts are used.

## Sources

- [Western Digital FD 179X-02 Floppy Disk Formatter/Controller Family data sheet, May 1980 (preliminary specification)](https://bitsavers.mirrorservice.org/components/westernDigital/FD179X-02_Data_Sheet_May1980.pdf) - 1-24 (pin connections and family table p1, pin outs p2-4, organisation p4-5, processor and disk interface p6-8, command description p8-16, formats p17-18, DC characteristics p18, timing p19-22, status register p23); FD1797-02
